text:
Predicates:
Timeless(x) ::: x is timeless.
DesignStyle(x, y) ::: x is a design style of y.
MassProductDesign(x) ::: x is a mass product design.
KellyWearstlerStyle(x) ::: x is a design style of Kelly Wearstler.
Evocative(x) ::: x is evocative.
Dreamy(x) ::: x is dreamy.
DesignBy(x, y) ::: x is a design by y.
Max(x) ::: x is Max.
Miroslav(x) ::: x is Miroslav Venhoda.
Music(x) ::: x is music.
Love(x, y) ::: x loves y.
Author(x, y) ::: x is the author of y.
Book(x) ::: x is a book.
Publish(x, y) ::: x is published in year y.
Specialize(x, y) ::: x specializes in y.
Renaissance(x) ::: x is Renaissance.
Baroque(x) ::: x is Baroque.
Czech(x) ::: x is Czech.
ChoralConductor(x) ::: x is a choral conductor.
Musician(x) ::: x is a musician.
∃x (ChoralConductor(x) → Musician(x)) ::: Any choral conductor is a musician.
∃x (Musician(x) ∧ Love(x, music)) ::: Some musicians love music.
Book(x) ∧ Author(miroslav, x) ∧ Publish(x, 1946) ::: Miroslav Venhoda published a book in 1946.
∃x (Czech(x) ∧ Author(x, y) ∧ Book(y) ∧ Publish(y, 1946)) ::: A Czech person wrote a book in 1946.
¬∃x (ChoralConductor(x) ∧ Specialize(x, renaissance)) ::: No choral conductor specialized in Renaissance.
Premises:
∀x (DesignStyle(x, miroslav) → Timeless(x)) ::: All of Zaha Hadid's design styles are timeless.
¬∃x (DesignStyle(x, y) ∧ MassProductDesign(x)) ::: No mass product design is timeless.
DesignStyle(zahaHadid, style1) ∨ DesignStyle(zahaHadid, style2) ::: Either Zaha Hadid's design style or Kelly Wearstler's design style.
∀x (DesignStyle(x, kellyWearstler) → Evocative(x)) ::: All of Kelly Wearstler's design styles are evocative.
∀x (DesignStyle(x, kellyWearstler) → Dreamy(x)) ::: All of Kelly Wearstler's design styles are dreamy.
∀x (DesignBy(max, x) ∧ Timeless(x) → (MassProductDesign(x) ∧ Evocative(x))) ::: If a design by Max is timeless, then it is a mass product design and evocative.
Conclusion:
∃x (DesignBy(max, x) ∧ Evocative(x) ∧ Dreamy(x)) ::: A design by Max is evocative and dreamy.
